correctness.rationale: Homogeneity identifies injective ordered tuple orbits with labeled finite induced \(C/D\) structures. The published \(C\)-relation model is a finite rooted binary-tree leaf structure; standard labeled rooted binary trees number \((2n-3)!!\), independently orienting the \(n-1\) internal vertices gives the plane count \(2^{n-1}(2n-3)!!=n!C_{n-1}\), and the unrooted labeled binary-tree count is \((2n-5)!!\) for \(n\ge3\). Root insertion has \(2n-3\) choices and equality patterns give the Stirling transform. The displayed sequences and ratios were independently replayed.

originality.rationale: The orbit formulas are direct consequences of prior structural identifications plus classical labeled-tree enumeration. Assari--Hosseinzadeh--Macpherson explicitly identify Aut(M4)=Aut(M,C), construct M6 from the homogeneous D-set with Aut(M6)=Aut(M,D), and record the strict M3<M4<M6 reduct chain. Bodirsky--Jonsson--Van Pham state that finite substructures of the homogeneous binary-branching C-relation are exactly leaf structures of finite rooted binary trees and that the underlying rooted tree is determined by its leaf relation. The remaining Catalan/double-factorial counts, two ratios, and Stirling transform are routine enumeration. Under the implication rule, an unstated corollary is covered.
residual_risks: Older oligomorphic-group literature may state the profiles explicitly, which would only strengthen rejection.
